reasons: Across 170 deterministic runs under equal tuning budgets, identical schedules, and the same data order, CauchyLift v0.3 beat tuned AdamW on 3 of the 4 predeclared workloads (W1 Small Decoder LM: 7.0413 vs 7.1080; W2 Medium Decoder LM: 7.0991 vs 7.1427; W3 Small ViT: 1.9107 vs 1.9226).

On high-dimensional neural network matrices, the additive Cauchy kernel denominator D_ij = RMS(G_{i,:}) + RMS(G_{:,j}) restores coordinate-wise Riemannian adaptation, resolving the v0.2 cotransverse complement degeneracy (where D_ij ≈ 2 ||G||_F^2 collapsed into NormalizedGD).
Embedding table energy starvation was eliminated by longest-fiber radius scaling rho(m, n) = sqrt(max(m, n)), restoring full step authority to vocabulary embedding matrices.

The mathematical foundation was formally verified in Lean 4 (formal/CauchyLift/Basic.lean and CauchyKernel.lean) with zero errors, proving exact degree-0 scale invariance, strict denominator positivity, coordinate magnitude bounds, and strict descent alignment.

The native ROCm/HIP multi-tensor kernel executes in 0.29–0.41 ms (within 1.2x of elementwise AdamW, 34x faster than Muon, and 57x faster than PyTorch reference), and full task-level gains survive the fused implementation.

On the held-out non-square ConvSSM workload (W4), CauchyLift v0.3 exhibited zero NaNs, zero loss spikes, and ultra-low cross-seed variance (7.6926 +/- 0.0016), supporting non-divergent generalization under zero tuning.
All gate requirements of Phase 5 are met; downstream scaling phases are unblocked.
